to: you, in almost all cases (see Notes)

variants.name: Bare string
variants.when: Older handlers: `socket.emit("game_response", "code")`. The string is the code. Several handlers send an object instead when the request has `request_id`.

variants.name: Failure
variants.when: `fail_response(code, place, data)`: a request failed. `place` defaults to the event name of the request.

variants.name: Success
variants.when: `success_response(code, place, data)`: a request succeeded. With an object as the first argument, `response` is `"data"`.

variants.name: Other object
variants.when: `socket.emit` or the `game_response` helper with an object: `response` and the fields of the code only. No `place`, `failed` or `success` unless the call site adds them. Hitchhiker codes (inside `player`) have this form.

variants.name: Skill result
variants.when: `skill`, `attack` and `heal`: the result object of the skill with `response: "data"` and `place` (the skill name). A failure has `failed: true` and `reason`. A success from `commence_attack` is the `Action` and has no `success` field.

variants.name: Condition
variants.when: `add_condition` gave you a condition. Always a hitchhiker in the next `player`, and often not a reply to a request: a skill of another character, a monster, or the server itself. During the anniversary event, each eligible character online when a round's host is picked gets `anniversary_visit` with `duration: 300000` (5 min), with no request. Some conditions are set without `add_condition` (for example `penalty_cd`) and do not send this code.

confirm.note: Live: `anniversary_visit` arrived unsolicited in `player.hitchhikers` on three characters at once

variants.name: Condition ended
variants.when: A condition of yours ran out (its `ms` reached 0) in the timer loop of the instance. Sent at once, not as a hitchhiker, and never as a reply to a request. A `player` update follows. Only for a condition in `G.conditions`, but also for one that came without a `condition` code, such as `penalty_cd` (added by teleports, magiport, equips and some item operations).

GameResponseCondition.summary: The `game_response` `condition`: a condition was put on you.
GameResponseCondition.description: Built by `add_condition` (node/server_functions.js:3236-3361) and pushed to `hitchhikers`, so it arrives inside the next `player`. Your `player.s[name]` has the same condition.

fields.name: cevent
fields.description: Always `true`: the official client fires the code event `condition`.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: The time of the condition, the same as `player.s[name].ms`: `duration` or `ms` of the call, else `G.conditions[name].duration`, else 1000. Never less than the time that the condition already had. Resistances can make it shorter, with a fraction.

fields.name: from
fields.description: Who gave the condition (`args.from.name` or `args.f`). Absent when the call site gives no source.

GameResponseConditionEnded.summary: The `game_response` `ex_condition`: a condition of yours ended.

GameResponseOther.summary: A `game_response` object that is not from `fail_response` or `success_response`.

fields.name: place
fields.description: The request, when the call site sets it.

fields.name: failed
fields.description: When the call site sets it.

fields.name: success
fields.description: When the call site sets it.

fields.name: cevent
fields.description: Asks the official client to fire a code event. `true` means the code is the event name.

fields.name: stale
fields.description: Hitchhiker results of a timer that ran while you were offline.

confirm.note: An open catch-all: some call site sets each listed field; others add their own

senders.what: `fail_response`, `success_response` and `game_response` helpers: the socket of the handler that runs now (`current_socket`).
A cave pause: most requests get `{response: "data", failed: true, reason: "cave_paused"}` (or `"cave_entering"`), with `place` and `request_id`.
Hitchhikers: some results wait in `player.hitchhikers` and arrive inside the next `player`.
